note: One implementation fast run passed 103/103 behavior cases but exceeded the 60s wall-clock ceiling at 60.15s; rendered assertions were consolidated into the existing browser case. Two orchestrator invariant attempts failed before product behavior because the fresh worktree first used system Python and then sandboxed local-server permissions; the same commits passed with the repository venv outside the sandbox. The known T-R27 worktree hook path issue also required two evidence-only commits to use --no-verify with the green formal gates named in their messages.

The mandatory second held-out probe ran RED on the property the A-plan calls inviolable: a wrong answer reported as success with all eight verdict checks green, reproduced 3x (probe rounds 1-2 with two different garbage strings, plus an independent orchestrator run f886ec29) on quotes.toscrape.com, the simplest possible page. The correct-answer rate also regressed, 2/8 (25%) at M5 to 1/7 (14%), against a stated goal of >=2x; published raw and unexplained. The owner's call was fix-both-then-freeze rather than freezing over a named hole. Both fixes are keyword screens on the task string, which is the third such screen this repo has shipped and the third whose ceiling is one rephrasing away (T-R31) - the probe falsified a limitation that M7 had declared and accepted only one milestone earlier. Round 1's two MEDIUMs were the same defect twice: code comments and analysis prose citing support-matrix declarations that did not exist (R1), and a fresh false-refusal cost shipped undeclared (R2). R5 is that defect's general form and is now T-R32. Criterion 5 is green OFFLINE only; the deployed URL serves main, so the live re-probe can only run after merge and redeploy, exactly as the M5 scope-screen fix was confirmed. A-freeze is not fully confirmed until that run.

Record-correction milestone opened by M10's own post-merge confirmation: ADR-015 had declared criterion 5 green offline with the live re-probe pending, that probe ran against merged main and refuted it, so every document implying A-freeze was making a claim the evidence contradicted. Three rounds, and each one found the same species of defect one level up from the last: R1 was two citations pointing at a renumbered task (the orchestrator's own miss during a mid-PR merge, and the merge commit message overclaimed the sweep); R2 was a guard that only appeared to guard - a 5-file, 4-literal-phrase allowlist; R4 was that guard still missing the identical phrase split by markdown bold; R5 was the widened guard excluding the very file whose live claim had demonstrated the hole. The pattern worth keeping: every round, the fix's stated ceiling was narrower than the real one, and the review's job was closing that gap rather than finding new bugs. Three id collisions from concurrent sessions during one task (M30 taken by PR #24, M32/M33 landed mid-flight) forced the responsiveness block to renumber to M34 - the block renumbered, not the branch. T-R33 was logged in round 1 and removed in round 2 when the repair satisfied its acceptance outright; net debt 0. The tasks/ scan exclusion survives as a declared tradeoff after the narrower quote-strip fix was tried and verified insufficient. This PR corrects the record only - the responsiveness defect itself is M34.

Closes the defect M10's probe found and M10's own fix did not: a grounded-but-unresponsive string reported as success. Deliberately not a fourth keyword screen — this repo had shipped three (log into, delete all, which...most) and a probe falsified each. The mechanism is cross-page site-invariance: a value whose local neighbourhood also appears on another page the run visited is chrome, not an answer. Each round attacked the heuristic's false-positive side and each repair made it narrower rather than more declared: R1 (HIGH) showed the first cut failed a CORRECT title on the listing->detail shape, the commonest navigation pattern in the domain, so the fix moved from comparing the bare value to comparing its local context — and that let the numeric exemption be deleted outright, closing a declared ceiling instead of adding one. R2-1 showed the context window anchored on the first textual occurrence, fixed by threading the real DOM offset through from agent.py. R2-2 was a false 'confirmed by curl' fixture-parity claim (35 of 50 categories, order broken) in two documents of record. R2-3, found by the orchestrator rather than the reviewer, was per-round repair narrative and a superseded gate number bled into the support matrix — blocking by the protocol's own scope rule regardless of severity. gate_failures 1 is the pre-commit hook's wall-clock straddle of the 60s local ceiling under external load (ADR-013's named band), which forced one documented --no-verify commit; the suite scored 1.000 throughout and the orchestrator re-ran the gate independently. Criterion 5 stays RED: this is demonstrated offline only, and the repeated-run confirmation against the redeployed build is the one remaining acceptance item, structurally impossible pre-merge.

First paid component in the verifier, after four structural mechanisms against the same defect were each falsified by real input (log into, delete all, which...most, M34's context window - the last refuted by its own post-merge confirmation, 6 wrong-answer-as-success in 9 deployed runs). Owner chose an LLM judge; it is wired as the LAST rung of the ladder, one call per run at the terminal-verdict boundary, injected in the stub_planner shape so the offline gate still reports cost $0.0000 across 45 stubbed calls. Measured ladder: 4/48 verdicts rejected by L1 alone, judge reached 44/48. Round 1's HIGH is the milestone's own lesson: bool(parsed['certify']) made the string 'false' truthy, so a judge that REJECTED would silently certify - the exact inversion of the guarantee the task exists to provide, and invisible because every judge case used the stub and no case had ever executed live_judge's real parser. The repair closed the class, not the line: the real parse path is now under test with only the transport mocked. R2 was the prompt fence being forgeable by page text containing the literal marker, with the injection case's own assertion using find() where the attack needs rfind() - the test blind in the same direction as the bug, twice in one PR. R3 was the strict fix's own undeclared cost: is True also rejects {'certify': 'true'}, whose failure mode is not one bad run but the agent certifying nothing at all; declared as D26 in D22's template and pinned by a scenario, with provider-side response_format enforcement routed to debt T-R33 rather than guessed at. Fourth undeclared-over-refusal finding on this repo (PR #25 R2, PR #30 R1, here). human_interventions 1 is the owner's mechanism decision. NOT verified here: no OPENROUTER_API_KEY in this environment, so the live judge's grading QUALITY is untested - only its wiring. Criterion 5 stays RED until the post-merge repeated-run confirmation, and this time the record says so before the check rather than after.

The planner-side half of the aggregate hole M10's probe opened: `extract_all` as a comparison primitive, a deterministic site-agnostic plan lint, and ranking kept in code. Five rounds, two circuit breakers, and the same species of defect regenerated four times — a silent success where a raw enumeration is published as the answer to a single-answer question (R2 -> R9 -> R16 -> R20). Each repair moved the decision point rather than closing it: `is_aggregate` as the gate over-corrected and dropped every 'cheapest' wording; a `\b(list|every|each)\b` heuristic replaced it and got the call backwards on 'Check each product and tell me which one is the cheapest'; the third fix deleted the guessing entirely and made the planner DECLARE `rank: true|false`, which is the right shape and still shipped a hole because code held both halves of the contradiction and compared them nowhere. The fourth fix closed it, and immediately produced R27's undeclared false refusal on a plural which-question — logged, not hidden. Worth keeping: three of the five rounds were spent on wall-clock ceilings, not on the feature. The local `fast` gate went non-deterministic mid-loop (60.24s vs 60 with 109/109 passing, refusing a docs-only commit), the fix for that moved cost into `invariant` and broke CI at 15.06s vs 15, and the fix for THAT published a band no reader could reproduce from the ledger committed beside it. gate_failures 2 are those two. Both circuit breakers went to the human, who ruled 'amend the ceiling' and then 'last round'; per that ruling five findings ship as named debt (T-R34..T-R38) rather than a sixth round. rejected 1 is the T-RANK-MIRROR direction, accepted by the reviewer on its merits: code has no non-guessing predicate for 'this task wants the whole set', and the only candidate is the wording regex R16 deleted for getting exactly this call backwards. `live-books-cheapest-travel` was never run — it is `full`-tagged and costs money — so the claim that a real planner emits a correct `rank` has no eval evidence, and ADR-016 says so plainly instead of implying otherwise.
